ASSESSMENT

Patient is a 70-year-old with a history of anemia who presented with troponin elevation. Initial troponin was elevated; repeat troponin rose to 0.9. Cardiology was consulted and agrees this represents an acute non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). The clinical picture is most consistent with demand ischemia in the setting of anemia with superimposed acute coronary syndrome. Management will proceed with anticoagulation and cardiology co-management.

PLAN

1. Initiate heparin per protocol for NSTEMI.
2. Continue cardiology consultation and co-management.
3. Monitor troponin trend and clinical response to anticoagulation.

TESTING RESULTS

Hemoglobin 7.1 (down from 9.0 on admission). Melena noted on gastrointestinal examination.

ASSESSMENT

Patient is a 67-year-old with dark stools who presented with an upper gastrointestinal bleed. Hemoglobin has declined from 9.0 to 7.1, and gastrointestinal examination revealed melena. The clinical picture is consistent with an upper gastrointestinal bleed, likely related to iron supplementation as a contributing factor. Endoscopy is planned for tomorrow to identify and treat the bleeding source.

PLAN

1. Initiate pantoprazole drip for upper gastrointestinal bleed.
2. Schedule esophagogastroduodenoscopy for tomorrow.

Confusion — New onset. Urinalysis was clean. Sodium level 128. Assessment: hyponatremia as likely etiology of confusion. Fluid restriction initiated. Sodium recheck planned for Friday.

Not documented.

Assessment and Plan

Hyponatremia with associated confusion. The resident presented with new confusion. Urinalysis was negative, ruling out urinary tract infection as the cause. Serum sodium of 128 indicates hyponatremia as the likely etiology of the acute mental status change. Fluid restriction has been implemented to address the low sodium. Sodium level will be rechecked on Friday to assess response to intervention and guide further management.

Plan:

1. Implement fluid restriction for hyponatremia.
2. Recheck serum sodium on Friday.
3. Monitor mental status for improvement with sodium correction.
